claims.text: The GI application says that in Bareilly cane and bamboo, and in one passage also wood, are the most commonly used materials for making furniture and household items needed in daily life.

quotes.quote: In the Bareilly, Cane and Bamboo furniture are the most commonly used materials to make various types of furniture and house hold items which are essential for daily life
Cane and Bamboo are the most commonly used materials to make furniture and house hold items which are essential for daily life.
In the Bareilly, Cane, Bamboo and wooden furniture are the most commonly used materials to make various types of furniture and house hold items

claims.text: A Bareilly furniture frame is made of thick bamboo by heating, bending and joining, and is finally rounded with thin processed cane called gola.

quotes.quote: Furniture frame is made with thick bamboo by heating, bending and joining. Finally, the frame is rounded with thin processed cane called 'Gola'.
The production of furniture involves different stages such as frame making with bamboo, polishing and rounding with processed thin cane.

claims.text: According to the GI application, the furniture is strong because bamboo forms the body structure while cane is used for binding and for weaving the seat.

quotes.quote: It is strong because bamboo is used in the body structure while the cane is used in binding as well as weaving the seating part of the furniture.

claims.text: The Bareilly district administration describes Bareilly as a production centre for cane (bans) furniture.

quotes.quote: Although Bareilly is a production center for cane (bans) furniture
Bareilly is famous as a production center for cane furniture.

claims.text: The GI application says Bareilly's furniture artisans work in three raw materials, bamboo, cane and wood, with hundreds of varieties in each.

quotes.quote: they are producing 3 different type of raw material furniture with the hundreds of variety in each category of raw material like bamboo, cane, and wood

claims.text: Products named in the GI application include sofas, chairs, racks, tables, swing chairs, stools, beds, jhoola, diwan sets, coffee tables and dining tables.

quotes.quote: The rich quality products include sofas, chairs, racks, tables and swing chairs. Stools, Beds, Jhoola, Diwan set, Sethi, Coffee table, Dining table, Table, Chair

claims.text: Bareilly's artisans also make decorative and everyday items in bamboo and cane, such as lamps, garden chairs, indoor and outdoor jhula and hanging items.

quotes.quote: make the variety of decorative item in the bamboo and cane including various type of usefull products for the education as well as decoration and daily need purpose like the lamps. gardem chairs, various type of jhula for outdoor and indoor purpose, different type of hanging items
Articles such as furniture, dustbins, racks, lamps, baskets, pot holders, sofa sets and center tables are part of the huge repertoire of items produced.

claims.text: A 2025 field study describes Bareilly district of Uttar Pradesh as renowned for its bamboo handicrafts.

quotes.quote: particularly in areas such as the Bareilly district of Uttar Pradesh, which is renowned for its bamboo handicrafts

quotes.quote: The tradition of cane and bamboo work started nearly 100 years back and carried from older generations to younger generations.

claims.text: The Imperial Gazetteer of India noted Bareilly city for its furniture, made both of bamboo and of the ordinary timbers used for furniture.

quotes.quote: Bareilly is also noted for its furniture, made both of bamboo and of the ordinary timbers in use for this purpose.
Bareilly city is noted for the production of furniture.

quotes.quote: The prefix is now usually interpreted as being the word bans or ' bamboo,' and is still used by the inhabitants.

it was named for two princes: Bansaldev and Baraldev, sons of Jagat Singh Katehriya, who founded the city in 1537

claims.text: Thick cane is used to make the frame of an article or piece of furniture, while pencil cane is used for designing and binding.

quotes.quote: The thick cane is used for making frame of an article or furniture where as pencil cane is used for designing and binding purpose.

claims.text: Mota cane, meaning thick cane, is added to the furniture for better support.

quotes.quote: Adding mota cane (thick cane) to the furniture for better support.

quotes.quote: Cane and bamboo products at Bareilly are very strong, durable and eco-friendly.

claims.text: In Bareilly, furniture is made using bamboo because bamboo is flexible.

quotes.quote: In Bareilly, Furniture is made using bamboo as it is flexible.

claims.text: Slicing runs lengthwise along the densely packed fibres and is a fairly smooth operation, needing only the requisite amount of moisture in the culm.

quotes.quote: Slicing is done longitudinally along the length of the densely packed fibres and a fairly smooth operation, requiring only the requisite amount of moisture in the Culm.

claims.text: The cane is heated on a slow fire, generally with a kerosene lamp, for flexibility before it is bent into shape.

quotes.quote: The cane is heated on a slow fire, generally with a kerosene lamp for flexibility.
A kerosene lamp is used to heat the cane before it can be bent into shape.

claims.text: The bamboo stick is heated with a kerosene lamp and bent to the desired shape; heated bamboo is easy to bend.

quotes.quote: Then the bamboo stick is heated using kerosene lamp and it is bent as per the desired shape. Heated bamboo is easy to bend.

claims.text: Production of cane products goes through various stages, beginning with the collection of raw material from the forests.

claims.text: To obtain a smooth surface, the upper layer of the raw cane collected from the forests is scraped off.

claims.text: The long cane sticks are cut into smaller pieces, followed by splitting the cane into thin strips that can be split as thin as required.

quotes.locator: Application 926, method of production, techniques, p. 33
quotes.quote: The long cane sticks are cut into smaller pieces that are followed by splitting the cane to obtain thin strips. Cane can be further split, making it as thin as required.

claims.text: The split cane is bent with a blowlamp into the shape needed for the furniture or article, which may cause burns on the surface that are removed by rubbing with sandpaper.

quotes.locator: Application 926, method of production, techniques, p. 33
quotes.quote: The split cane is now bent using a blowlamp that may cause some burns on the surface; these are removed by rubbing with sandpaper.

claims.text: Following this, the cane can be woven according to the design of the articles being made from it.

quotes.locator: Application 926, method of production, techniques, p. 33
quotes.quote: Following this, the cane can be woven based on the design of the articles being fashioned from it.

claims.text: After the finishing touches, the products may be dabbed with a coat of varnish before they are dispatched to the market.

quotes.locator: Application 926, method of production, techniques, p. 33

claims.text: Craftsmen cut bamboo to the desired lengths with cutting tools called dao, and cut it to size by thickness with different kinds of knives.

lede.text: The GI application says that in Bareilly, Uttar Pradesh, cane and bamboo, and in one passage also wood, are the most commonly used materials for furniture and household items needed in daily life.
The GI application makes the furniture frame of thick bamboo by heating, bending and joining (another passage says thick cane), finally rounded with thin processed cane called gola.

The district administration calls Bareilly a production centre for cane (bans) furniture, and the GI journal text of December 2023 says nearly 1500 artisans are engaged in furniture work in Bareilly in bamboo, cane and wood.

Bareilly Cane & Bamboo Craft, which the GI registry's record names Bareilly Furniture, is GI application 926, advertised in Geographical Indications Journal 187 and registered with certificate 639 on 16 April 2024.

sentences.text: Sources differ on when cane and bamboo work began in Bareilly: the GI application says nearly 80 to 100 years ago, or nearly 100 in another passage, while the Imperial Gazetteer and Nevill's 1911 gazetteer already record bamboo furniture and carpenters working in bamboo there.

The application also says Bareilly's furniture is of different shapes, sizes, qualities and designs from centuries, and calls Bareilly a hub of wooden and cane-bamboo furniture before British reign in India.

In 1911 Nevill recorded about 1,500 persons employed in furniture manufacture, as a rule in workshops owned by dealers, and wrote that this industry of work in wood was, in its form then, of fairly recent origin.
Writing of Bareilly's work in wood, Nevill said that in old days Bareilly was celebrated for lacquered and gilt furniture, and that its painted woodwork had either disappeared or degenerated.

Sources differ on the name Bans Bareilly: the GI application ties it to bans craft, plentiful bamboo and a big bamboo market, while the district administration says it is not derived from the bans market.
Among these accounts, the GI application, Wikipedia and the district administration say Jagat Singh Katehriya founded Bareilly, or its earliest settlement, in 1537 and named it after his two sons.
According to the Imperial Gazetteer, the prefix Bans was then usually interpreted as bans, bamboo, while the district administration writes of cane (bans) furniture.
Production of cane products begins with the collection of raw material from the forests, and the upper layer of the raw cane is scraped off for a smooth surface.
The long cane sticks are cut into smaller pieces and split into thin strips, and whole stems are cut with a hacksaw and split with a billhook or dao.
The split cane is bent with a blowlamp, which may cause burns on the surface, and these are removed by rubbing with sandpaper.
Bamboo is immersed in water for 2 hours, heated with a kerosene lamp, bent to shape and shaped properly with a wooden tool called mungri.
Cane is joined to the bamboo with thin small nails, and the joints are blended with strips of pencil cane.
The cane is wrapped around the bamboo frame by weaving, a rounding process locally called binayi, so that the frame inside cannot be seen from outside.
Finally the items are cleaned with sandpaper and polished with varnish before being dispatched to the market.
The GI application lists bamboo, cane, cane peel, desi cane, plywood, nails and gola cane wire as raw materials.

While one passage makes the furniture frame of thick bamboo, the GI application also says thick cane is used for making the frame of an article or furniture, and pencil cane for designing and binding.
Mota cane, meaning thick cane, is added to the furniture for better support.
Bamboo also comes to Bareilly from Assam as a raw material, the GI application says.
The GI application calls the cane and bamboo products very strong, durable and eco-friendly, made of organic, natural material.
Furniture is made using bamboo because it is flexible, and heated bamboo is easy to bend.
The cane is heated on a slow fire, generally with a kerosene lamp, for flexibility before it is bent into shape.
Slicing runs lengthwise along the densely packed fibres and is fairly smooth, needing only the requisite amount of moisture in the culm.
According to the GI application, the artisans create their motif patterns from their own imagination and skill without any traced design.
The GI application names the surahi-matka shape made for the back of a chair as one of the popular motifs available in the market.
Artisans use many natural patterns without any colour, and make traditional as well as contemporary furniture with modern designs for the global market.
The GI application calls the woven cane and bamboo sofa sets and chairs remarkable among all its products, and the attractive intricate design patterns admirable for their uniqueness.
NewsClick reported that artisans have changed designs and diversified products to compete with wooden furniture.
Modern Gramodyog Sewa Sansthan filed GI application 926 on 18 July 2022, and it was advertised in Geographical Indications Journal 187 dated 15 December 2023.
The registry records certificate 639 dated 16 April 2024, valid up to 17 July 2032, and numbers its authorised users up to 8.

The GI journal text of December 2023 says nearly 1500 artisans are engaged in furniture work in Bareilly in bamboo, cane and wood, or in cane and bamboo furniture work in another passage, and a 2025 study reports over 500 cane and bamboo workers at Fatehganj, including 400 female artisans.
NewsClick reported that Bareilly's cane furniture was once a favourite of middle-class families for its affordable price, elegant look and low maintenance.
The 2025 study found that women artisans face economic limits, a lack of market access, limited education and little technical skill, and that many have low incomes and limited access to credit.
